Yes. I’d focus on small/boutique studios that will audit the existing site and booking journey, rather than immediately trying to sell you a full rebuild.

My Toronto shortlist

ThrillX Design — best for UX/conversion diagnosis. They specifically emphasize conversion-optimized websites, UX strategy, CRO, messaging, and measurable outcomes such as bookings. Good fit if people are visiting but failing to understand where/how to book.

CanConnect Studio — best for a straightforward small-business review. It’s a founder-led Toronto studio that explicitly offers free website reviews and focuses on unclear booking/contact processes. 
Can Connect Studio

Frontline Studio — best if you're a local service business. They specifically offer a free audit of existing sites covering mobile experience, lead generation and conversion issues, with a strong booking-first approach. 
Frontline Studio

SimpleStart Digital — best if you want an inexpensive first diagnosis. Their “Digital Snapshot” reviews the website's first impression and gives next-step recommendations, while their higher-tier “Lead Engine” specifically addresses CTAs, contact flow and conversion. 
SimpleStart Digital

Brand Vision Marketing - Web Design & Branding — best for a broader UX/brand audit. Their audits are positioned around website/UX/SEO issues and a prioritized roadmap rather than simply redesigning pages.

Mojo Media Web Design — best for a boutique design/UX perspective. They focus on custom, conversion-oriented websites for small-to-mid-sized businesses, with usability, hierarchy and calls-to-action built into their approach.

Who I'd contact first

For your particular problem — “we have a website, but people don't know how to book” — I'd start with ThrillX, CanConnect, and Frontline. They appear particularly aligned with diagnosing the conversion path rather than just making the website prettier.

When contacting them, ask for a paid or free 30–60 minute booking-flow audit, and specifically request that they test:

Can a first-time visitor find “Book” within 5–10 seconds?

Is the booking CTA visible on mobile?

Is it obvious what happens after clicking?

Are there too many choices before booking?

Does the booking page reinforce trust and answer key objections?

Where are visitors likely abandoning the process?

What 3 changes would they make without rebuilding the whole site?

That last question is important: it will quickly distinguish a studio that can diagnose the problem from one that simply wants to sell you a new website.

ChatGPT can make mistakes. Check important info.
